transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with the pre-trade huddle. We need to finalize the collateral reinvestment plan for the $25 million in cash collateral from our securities-lending book. The draft on the table proposes investing the full amount in 30-day commercial paper issued by Delta Financial. Before I make my decision, I'd like to hear from each of you on exceptions or concerns. Let's start with counterparty risk, then compliance, client coverage, and investment operations. Please keep it to one minute each.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical exception. I completed a counterparty review this morning and confirmed that Delta Financial's commercial paper is under active rating review. Until that review closes, desk policy prohibits any new purchase of Delta commercial paper. I recorded the result in my working file, but I should note the counterparty system has not been updated yet, so it may not be visible to everyone. My recommendation is that we do not proceed with investing the $25 million in Delta Financial commercial paper until the rating review is closed and the prohibition is lifted.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compliance exception. I reviewed the applicable collateral-investment mandate this week, and it restricts cash collateral investments to government Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit only, each with a maximum maturity of 14 days. The draft plan to invest in 30-day commercial paper issued by Delta Financial violates this mandate on multiple grounds: commercial paper is not a permitted instrument, the 30-day maturity exceeds the 14-day limit, and Delta Financial's credit rating does not meet the AAA requirement. I should also note that this restriction has not yet been added to the desk's pre-trade checklist, which is why it wasn't caught earlier in the process. My recommendation is that we do not proceed with the Delta Financial commercial paper plan and instead restrict our collateral reinvestment to qualifying Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank CDs with maturities of no more than 14 days.

transcript.text: I have an operations update to share. I confirmed with the settlement team today that our platform can process exactly $12,000,000 of Treasury bills and $6,000,000 of AAA bank certificates of deposit on a T+1 basis, with daily position reconciliation. This capacity confirmation is documented in an operations note that has not yet been circulated to the rest of the desk. Given the exceptions raised by counterparty risk, compliance, and client coverage, this is directly relevant: compliance has restricted us to Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank CDs with maturities of 14 days or less, and client coverage has told us to hold back $7,000,000, leaving $18,000,000 to invest. Our confirmed operational capacity of $12 million in T-bills plus $6 million in AAA bank CDs totals exactly $18,000,000, which matches the investable amount after the client's cash holdback. My recommendation is that we allocate $12,000,000 to Treasury bills and $6,000,000 to AAA bank certificates of deposit, all with maturities of 14 days or less, with $7,000,000 remaining as uninvested cash.
